name: Eindhoven University of Technology
summary: Technical university in Eindhoven; 13 English-taught BSc programmes, from applied physics to industrial design, all asking for Maths AA HL.

ib.text: Full IB Diploma with Maths AA HL for every bachelor's; engineering and design ones add Physics HL. An IB Diploma taught only in English, or English A HL at 5, covers English.

apply.via: Studielink, then TU/e's OSIRIS application form

dates.label: Selection programmes: complete application and fee paid, 23:59 CET
All other programmes: complete application, 23:59 CET

programmes.name: Applied Mathematics
programmes.about: Mathematics used to model real problems from industry and government, from image processing to supply chains, then calculated and solved; you learn to work with specialists from other fields.
programmes.overview: You learn to build a mathematical model of a practical problem, solve it, and translate the answer back so specialists in other fields can use it, with examples from mobile technology, cybersecurity, logistics, medical imaging and car design. Teaching follows challenge-based learning: lectures and small-group practical sessions, with problems tackled in groups and project work growing over the three years. Besides compulsory mathematics courses you take non-technology courses and a large share of free electives, and a double bachelor with Applied Physics or Computer Science and Engineering is possible. Graduates become cryptologists, logistics consultants, statisticians and software designers, or continue to a two-year master's.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the subject requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May and complete the study-choice check.

programmes.name: Applied Physics
programmes.ib: Maths AA HL and Physics HL.
programmes.about: Light and sound, flow and heat, atoms and particles, studied to find nature's laws and turn them into technology, with an emphasis on applying physics in Eindhoven's high-tech setting.
programmes.overview: You study the physics of light and sound, flow and heat, atoms and particles, and build skills in experimental design, data handling, automation and computational physics. About three quarters of the programme is core physics and mathematics, and a quarter is electives that deepen physics or reach into other TU/e fields, with courses on the impact of technology. Teams tackle technological and societal challenges, and you can join student teams such as Solid or Polar. The programme ends with a Bachelor End Project, either in a research group or on an open problem from companies or student teams. Graduates enter a master's such as Applied Physics, Nuclear Fusion or quantum science, or work in chip manufacturing and research institutes.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the subject requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May and complete the study-choice check.

programmes.name: Architecture, Urbanism and Building Sciences
programmes.ib: Maths AA HL and Physics HL. Numerus fixus: apply by 15 January; ranked on grades, an online test (13 March 2027) and a campus day (3 April 2027).
programmes.about: How buildings, neighbourhoods and cities are designed, built and reshaped: architecture, urban design and building physics and technology in one mix of design studio and theory.
programmes.overview: The programme joins architecture, urbanism, building sciences, structural design and real estate, looking at how the living environment is built and keeps changing. You can follow one of three profiles from the start, building physics and structural design, architectural urban design and engineering, or urban systems and real estate, and choose electives to shape your own route. Teaching mixes lectures, guided self-study and challenge-based design projects done in multidisciplinary teams, starting with a first-year studio. Year two builds the structural engineering core, and year three is dominated by a final project. Graduates continue to a master's and work in architecture firms, construction, housing associations and government.
programmes.selectionNote: Numerus fixus: apply by 15 Jan. 2026 rules: grades 2/3, online test 1/3; 2027 adds an online test (13 Mar) and campus day (3 Apr), full criteria not yet published.

programmes.name: Automotive Technology
programmes.ib: Maths AA HL and Physics HL.
programmes.about: The car as one connected high-tech system: electronics, motion and control for hybrid, electric and self-driving vehicles. Formally a major of Electrical Engineering, and the degree is a BSc Electrical Engineering.
programmes.overview: You study the car as a system, combining mechanical engineering with electronics and software for electric, automated and connected vehicles. Half of the curriculum is automotive courses and half is core subjects such as mathematics, natural sciences and multidisciplinary design, with a quarter given to electives. A learning pathway on users, society and enterprise looks at the impact of technology on people. Teaching is lectures, guided self-study and challenge-based projects on real cases, ending with an individual Bachelor End Project. The degree is awarded as electrical engineering with an automotive specialisation, and the Brainport Eindhoven region, home to much of the Dutch automotive industry, provides employers.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the subject requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May and complete the study-choice check.

programmes.name: Chemical Engineering and Chemistry
programmes.ib: Maths AA HL, Physics and Chemistry, one of them HL. Numerus fixus: apply by 15 January; ranked on grades and an online test (20 March 2027).
programmes.about: Chemistry and process engineering for new materials, cleaner energy and medicines, in the English-taught track; the bilingual Scheikundige Technologie has the same courses and no selection.
programmes.overview: You combine chemistry, materials science and process engineering, from how molecules are built to scaling a process up to continuous production. Year one stresses mathematics and physics with inorganic, physical and bio-chemistry, and lab sessions right after lectures. Year two adds kinetics, polymer chemistry, separation technology and challenge-based projects on societal issues, and year three is an independent final project in a research group. From year two you pick electives, including themes such as AI, energy and sustainability, and take ethics-of-technology courses. Most students go on to a master's, and the degree is internationally accredited by the IChemE.

needs.note: Physics or Chemistry must be HL; the other can be SL.
Physics or Chemistry must be HL; the other can be SL.

programmes.selectionNote: Numerus fixus: apply by 15 Jan 2027. Ranked on an online cognitive test on 20 March (60%) and your grades (40%); the motivation questionnaire must be done on time.

programmes.name: Computer Science and Engineering
programmes.ib: Maths AA HL. Numerus fixus: apply by 15 January; ranked on grades and an online selection day (6 March 2027).
programmes.about: How to design, build and reason about software systems and web services, including proving programs correct and efficient with formal mathematical methods, with the user kept in view.
programmes.overview: After a base of calculus, statistics, linear algebra and logic, you follow three learning lines throughout: systems (security, networks, databases), software development, and algorithms and theory of computing. In year one you build a user-friendly web portal; in year two you work with students from other programmes on an open problem tied to the Sustainable Development Goals; in year three you take an in-depth course and join a ten-week group project on open-source software before the Bachelor Final Project. Two courses cover engineering ethics and engineering for society. Graduates become software or app developers, or take a master's in Computer Science and Engineering or Embedded Systems.
programmes.selectionNote: Numerus fixus: apply by 15 Jan 2027. Online tests on 6 March: logical reasoning 40%, algorithmic thinking 40%; your average grade 10% and maths grade 10%.

programmes.name: Data Science
programmes.about: Statistics, programming, data mining and business analytics plus the law and ethics of data, in a joint degree with Tilburg University taught in both Eindhoven and Tilburg. Apply through TU/e.
programmes.overview: This is a joint programme of Eindhoven and Tilburg, so you attend classes at both universities. It is organised in six learning lines: law and ethics, computer science, business, data analytics, data challenges and cognitive science, with courses in statistics, programming, data mining and business analytics. In the data challenges line, teams solve real problems using large data sets from different fields. Electives let you aim for a master's, for example through packages in advanced data science or finance and risk, or minors in business and entrepreneurship or cognitive science and AI. The programme ends with a Bachelor End Project and leads to master's degrees in data science, business analytics or marketing analytics.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the subject requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May and complete the study-choice check.

programmes.name: Electrical Engineering
programmes.ib: Maths AA HL and Physics HL.
programmes.about: Electricity and magnetism put to work in chips, motors and wireless energy, organised around three first-year themes such as the connected world, from photonic chips to wifi.
programmes.overview: You learn the fundamentals of electricity and magnetism through three societal themes: communication, such as chips using light signals and wireless protocols, healthcare, such as MRI scanners and electromagnetic therapies, and sustainable energy systems. Half of the curriculum is electrical engineering major subjects, the rest core subjects and a quarter electives, plus a pathway on the impact of technology on society. Teaching combines lectures, guided self-study and challenge-based projects, supported by part-time professors, guest lectures and excursions with companies in the Brainport Eindhoven region. Each student completes an individual Bachelor End Project.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the subject requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May and complete the study-choice check.

programmes.name: Industrial Design
programmes.ib: Maths AA HL and Physics HL.
programmes.about: Designing interactive products, systems and services that combine technology, data, users and aesthetics, learned mostly through design projects: smart homes, intelligent clothing, health and play.
programmes.overview: You learn to turn technology into products and services, balancing data, creativity, user needs, aesthetics, social impact and business across five areas: business and entrepreneurship, creativity and aesthetics, math, data and computing, technology and realization, and user and society. Learning is self-directed and hands-on, with prototypes made to test ideas and multidisciplinary squads working on social themes and presenting at a Demo Day each semester. From year two you deepen your strongest area, using electives in design or other departments. Year three brings an exchange, internship or minor elsewhere, then a Final Bachelor Project. Graduates become product, UX and service designers, innovation consultants or entrepreneurs.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the subject requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May and complete the study-choice check.

programmes.name: Industrial Engineering
programmes.about: Business processes treated as systems to analyse, model and improve, from logistics and planning to human behaviour and data-driven decisions, through projects with industry partners.
programmes.overview: You treat business processes as systems that can be analysed, modelled and improved, using mathematics, data science and AI models. The core covers occupational and organisational psychology, operational management, product innovation and information systems, alongside statistics, data engineering and an ethics course on the impact of technology. Teaching includes field trips, company partnerships, a multidisciplinary challenge-based project in year two and many electives, half of year three, to broaden or deepen your studies. The degree ends with a final project at an external organisation, where you answer a research question about a business case.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the subject requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May and complete the study-choice check.

programmes.name: Mechanical Engineering
programmes.ib: Maths AA HL and Physics HL. Numerus fixus: apply by 15 January; ranked only on online selection tests (13 March 2027), not grades.
programmes.about: Designing and building products, machines and production processes, drawing on maths, physics and chemistry, with much of the learning done in project teams.
programmes.overview: You combine mathematics, physics and chemistry with heat and flow, mechanics, dynamics, control theory and material properties, to design and improve mechanical products and production processes. Year one includes CAD and NX training for 3D design, year two adds thermodynamics and the control of mechanical systems, and about 30 percent of the curriculum is challenge-based projects tackled in groups. Year three offers electives and a Bachelor Final Project in a faculty research group, with past topics including humanoid robots and chip factory modelling. Graduates work in machine manufacturing, research institutes, start-ups and multinationals.
programmes.selectionNote: Numerus fixus: apply by 15 Jan 2027. Ranked only on online tests on 13 March: maths 25%, physics 25%, a programme-content test 50%. Grades do not count.

programmes.name: Psychology & Technology
programmes.about: Psychology applied to technology: how people use and are affected by technology, and how to design new applications with that knowledge, through small-scale challenge-based projects.
programmes.overview: You study how technology shapes people and how to design technology around human needs, for example household robots, smart lighting and intelligent infrastructure. Year one is a fixed mix of about half psychology and half technology, with around two days a week on group design and research assignments. In the first quarter you choose a specialisation such as Robotics, ICT or Living, and from year two a quarter of the programme is free electives. Challenge-based projects bring in students from other departments, and year three ends with an individual Bachelor End Project including a scientific report.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the subject requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May and complete the study-choice check.

programmes.name: Sustainable Innovation
programmes.about: How sustainable technology actually gets adopted: costs, risks, regulation and social acceptance, seen from the side of citizens, government and companies, in Dutch and international context.
programmes.overview: The programme joins technology with sustainability, economics, policy and social science, to train people who can assess innovations and drive change. Three learning lines run through it: transitions, with courses such as Navigating Sustainability Transitions; assessment, using life-cycle assessment and cost-benefit analysis; and economic policy, including Economics of Innovation. You work on cases with companies, governments and societal organisations through challenge-based learning, and choose electives within the programme or from other TU/e programmes. Year three brings the perspectives together to assess innovations and support decisions, and the location in Brainport Eindhoven provides innovation partners.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the subject requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May and complete the study-choice check.

notes: A €100 non-refundable fee applies to each application from anyone schooled outside the Netherlands or at an international school there, so IB applicants pay it.
Biomedical Engineering and Medical Sciences and Technology are partly taught in Dutch and need proof of Dutch; Scheikundige Technologie is the bilingual twin of Chemical Engineering and Chemistry.
You need 45 of 60 credits in year 1 (binding study advice, 2026/27 rule), or you cannot re-enrol in that programme for three years.
